name: Perplexity
tagline: AI answer engine with web search, citations, and research modes

pricing.notes: Official pages checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $20/month or $200/year.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 5 Pro Searches/day; 3 file uploads/day; 40 MB/file; practically unlimited basic searches.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Higher Pro Search and file limits; 40 MB/file.

tiers.name: Education Pro
tiers.limits: Discounted Pro access for verified students and educators.
tiers.notes: No public annual price was found.

tiers.name: Enterprise Pro
tiers.limits: 500 Computer credits/month; 500 files/project; 15,000 persistent files/user; 100 session uploads/week; 50 MB/file.

tiers.name: Enterprise Max
tiers.limits: 15,000 Computer credits/month; 5,000 files/project; 50,000 persistent files/user; 1,000 session uploads/week.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for Pro, Max, and enterprise tiers; Education Pro is monthly; enterprise seats can mix Pro and Max
pricing.hiddenCosts: Computer credits expire at the end of each month and do not roll over. Refills and auto-refill are available; 100 credits are priced as $1. Upgrades can be prorated.

verdictSummary: A retrieval-plus-LLM answer engine is buildable, but Perplexity's search stack, source ranking, UX, mobile/browser surfaces, and model access make full parity hard.
coreLoopDIY: Search the web/API, fetch pages, rank passages, ask an LLM to answer with citations, and store threads.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because answers arrive fast with sources and fewer query-building chores.

priorArt.name: Perplexica
priorArt.desc: Open-source AI search engine inspired by Perplexity.

alternatives.name: GPT Researcher
alternatives.desc: A research agent rather than a search box; it returns cited reports and a bill from whichever model you chose.

facts.install: Clone/install the Python app or start its Docker Compose stack, then add model and search-provider keys
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini/Vertex, Azure, Bedrock, Cohere, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI, Ollama, vLLM, OpenRouter and other LangChain-backed providers; web retrieval commonly uses Tavily or another configured retriever
facts.dataFormat: Uploaded/local source files stay in the configured host folder and generated Markdown/PDF/DOCX reports are written under the host's outputs directory; search queries, scraped pages and prompts go to configured search/model services
facts.gapVsPaid: It produces deeper reports, but each answer is slower, more expensive to run, and less convenient than Perplexity's instant managed search experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Python or Docker is only the start: a non-expert must select compatible LLM, embedding and search providers, supply keys, and manage per-run API costs

alternatives.name: Khoj
alternatives.desc: A personal AI that searches the web and your files; broader than Perplexity, and noticeably heavier to run.

facts.install: Use the hosted app, or self-host the server with Docker or pip and optionally install its desktop/browser/Obsidian clients
facts.engines: Local OpenAI-compatible servers such as Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or vLLM, plus OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini and other cloud APIs
facts.dataFormat: Hosted accounts store chats and indexed documents in Khoj's cloud; self-hosting stores application data and vector embeddings in the operator's PostgreSQL/pgvector database while original synced files remain at their source
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a broader personal assistant, but its web-search freshness, source coverage, and answer-engine polish are weaker than Perplexity's managed index and research modes.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted app is immediate, but private self-hosting requires Docker or Python, PostgreSQL/pgvector, model configuration and an initial document index

alternatives.name: Local Deep Research
alternatives.desc: Less search box, more research intern: it searches, iterates and writes cited reports on your own hardware.

facts.install: Start the Docker Compose stack, or install the Python package and separately run an LLM endpoint and search backend
facts.engines: Ollama, llama.cpp/LM Studio and other OpenAI-compatible local endpoints plus cloud models; searches SearXNG, Wikipedia, arXiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, GitHub and optional paid search APIs
facts.dataFormat: Research history, settings, credentials and findings live in a per-user SQLCipher-encrypted SQLite database on the host; reports export as Markdown or PDF and indexed private documents remain local
facts.gapVsPaid: It is slower and substantially heavier to operate, especially with local models, than Perplexity's immediate search-and-answer workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The nominal quick start still means Docker plus an LLM model and usually SearXNG; local models need substantial RAM/VRAM and several gigabytes of disk

alternatives.name: Morphic
alternatives.desc: A cited answer engine with a prettier face; Docker quietly brings PostgreSQL, Redis and SearXNG along.

facts.install: Use the public hosted app, or clone the repo, set an AI key and run the official Docker Compose stack
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Ollama, Vercel AI Gateway and OpenAI-compatible providers; search through bundled SearXNG or Tavily, Brave, Exa and Firecrawl
facts.dataFormat: Current self-hosted chat history and accounts live in PostgreSQL, Redis supports runtime services, and optional uploads use configured object storage such as Cloudflare R2; hosted use stores the same classes of data in Morphic's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: It closely resembles the answer-engine experience, but has a smaller ecosystem and less mature reliability, indexing, and cross-device polish than Perplexity.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting launches PostgreSQL, Redis, SearXNG and the web app and still requires at least one model provider or a separately running Ollama instance

alternatives.name: Vane
alternatives.desc: Perplexity with the meter removed: cited answers and deep research, provided you can run one Docker stack.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image with one command; it bundles Vane and SearXNG
facts.engines: Local models through Ollama plus OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Groq and other cloud providers; web search through bundled SearXNG
facts.dataFormat: Search history and uploads are stored in the mounted local Docker volume; prompts leave the host only when a cloud model is selected
facts.gapVsPaid: It removes the subscription meter, but makes you operate the search stack and model backend instead of getting Perplexity's managed index, capacity, and reliability.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker, a persistent volume and either Ollama with a downloaded model or at least one cloud-model API key

rejectedAlternatives.name: Perplexity Standard
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Basic searches are practically unlimited; Pro Search and Research are explicitly very limited, which is the paid product's point.

notes: A nuanced kinda: there is real open-source prior art, but source quality and scale matter.
prompt:
Build me a personal answer engine like Perplexity, wrapping real search and LLM APIs,
not rebuilding them. Requirements:

- A local web app on localhost:3000: Node + Express + htmx, one input box, streamed
  answers.
- Per question: query the Brave Search API (key in .env), fetch the top 6 results with
  undici, extract readable text with @mozilla/readability + jsdom, then pass the
  question plus numbered excerpts to Claude or GPT (key in .env) with instructions to
  answer only from the excerpts and cite as [1][2].
- Render citations as footnote links; show the full source list under every answer.
- Follow-up questions stay in the same thread with prior Q&A in the context window.
- Threads stored in SQLite via better-sqlite3; a sidebar lists past threads by first
  question.
- If a page fails to fetch or extract, drop it and continue. Never cite a page that was
  not fetched.
- Binds to localhost only; no accounts, no telemetry, only the search and LLM calls
  leave my machine.
- Out of scope: crawling my own web index, model routing, and mobile apps. Answer
  quality tracks the search API, that is the deal.
- README: which keys to get (Brave Search has a free tier) and rough per-query cost.
